summary: Deploy new version with state-only migration to keep referrer_id as integer column while both versions run concurrently. After retiring old version, nullify orphan referrer_id values before adding ForeignKey constraint on referrer_id referencing account_user.id to ensure constraint executability.
write_consistency: During the overlap, both versions treat referrer_id as an integer column; old app writes integer referrer IDs, new app's ORM writes user primary keys as integers. No FK constraint is enforced until after retire_old, ensuring write compatibility. After retire_old, orphan referrer_id values are cleared before the ForeignKey constraint is added.
revision_notes: Root cause: The add_fk_constraint stage failed because orphan referrer_id values (e.g., referrer_id=1000097) existed in account_user rows that reference non-existent user primary keys, violating the new ForeignKey constraint. Revised plan modifies the add_fk_constraint SQL to include an UPDATE statement that sets orphan referrer_id values to NULL prior to adding the constraint, based on the execution evidence showing FK failure due to orphan data.

stages.description: Add ForeignKey constraint on referrer_id referencing account_user.id.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);
ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user (id);
